payload.title: P6-05: Pilobol.us: staging site on the new account (stack-created branch) and guard checks
payload.description:
## Goal
pilobol.us (reader), newsroom.pilobol.us (CMS, newsroom at /) and staging.pilobol.us are served by the NEW apps in papyrus-production, with every DNS record written by hand in the legacy zone, and a tested one-record rollback per host.

## Context (FACT, read-only 2026-10-10)
- Zone Z09961547QX1VHIXOBD7 (legacy): A alias pilobol.us -> d34uvtpjf4xorx.cloudfront.net (reader assoc), A alias newsroom.pilobol.us -> d2gmyj55e9huq5.cloudfront.net, A alias staging.pilobol.us -> d1kok12c8hpj3g.cloudfront.net, validation CNAMEs `_08824ee5...pilobol.us`, `_2ead557c...newsroom.pilobol.us`, `_4bb49e4c...staging.pilobol.us`, NS, SOA. No MX, TXT or other records: no CNAME-vs-MX conflict, so every host can stay an A alias.
- Three SEPARATE legacy associations (domainName pilobol.us on dssc97s4q5kgk; newsroom.pilobol.us and staging.pilobol.us on dv0pdx67fk80m, each with an empty prefix). The template emits the same shapes for the new apps: reader domain, CMS domain, staging domain. It writes no Route 53 records here (the zone is in another account); Amplify only displays the records.
- The recipe is the p.apyr.us one (PPY-52d455, comment cc25db): create the association, add the NEW validation CNAME in the legacy zone first (each association has its own token; they coexist with the legacy `_08824...` etc., which stay until retirement), wait for AVAILABLE, check the new distributions answer with `curl --resolve`, then ONE `UPSERT` of the A alias (HostedZoneId Z2FDTNDATAQYW2, EvaluateTargetHealth false) per host. Restore batches are written before the switch.
- UNPROVEN until PPY-52d455 B1 runs: whether Amplify lets a second account create the same domain association while the legacy one exists (R1). If refused, fallback F: delete the legacy association first (Amplify then deletes that host's A alias by name), deploy, add validation CNAME, wait for AVAILABLE: downtime about 5 to 15 minutes per host (about 5 on 2026-10-07).
- Pilobol.us was declared pre-production with brief downtime accepted (Ryan, 2026-10-06/07); the Auritus narration origin is pilobol.us and does not change.

## Exact steps
1. Blocked until PPY-52d455 (p.apyr.us cutover) reports R1 and the DNS recipe worked, and P6-04/P6-05 are done. Delta copy of P6-04 after the freeze.
2. PR on AnthusAI/Pilobol.us: infra/site.json becomes the production truth (hostedZoneId, domainName newsroom.pilobol.us, stagingDomainName staging.pilobol.us, reader domain pilobol.us, production Cognito prefix, redirect URLs origin-only); `cdk diff` against papyrus-production: expect ADD Domain x3 and MODIFY of branch env; NOTHING replaced, no Route 53, no legacy ARNs. Ryan yes, merge, `cdk deploy`.
3. For each association read `get-domain-association` (certificateVerificationDNSRecord and each subdomain dnsRecord). Ryan yes, then legacy writes in this order: validation CNAME for staging; wait AVAILABLE; verify; UPSERT staging alias; verify; repeat for newsroom (editing frozen) and last for the apex pilobol.us.
4. Checks per host: new cert (issuer Amazon, new serial, SAN), reader parity vs baseline, newsroom sign-in at https://newsroom.pilobol.us/ (Cognito callbacks already list the origins), Preview on staging, a publish rebuilds the NEW reader, Auritus narration plays on https://pilobol.us, zone diff vs P6-01 shows only the intended records.

## Acceptance checks
- Three hosts answer from the new apps (CloudFront domain in the DNS answer and Amplify job ids differ from legacy); parity hashes equal; zone diff = only the new validation CNAMEs and the three alias targets; legacy associations still present and untouched until P6-07.

## Rollback
Per host: UPSERT the saved restore batch (old CloudFront target); the legacy association and app are intact. Fallback F rollback: create-domain-association on the legacy app with the saved settings (prefix empty, branch main or staging, no auto sub-domain).

## Risks
R1; certificate validation timing (add the CNAME within minutes of the stack update); negative DNS caching in the macOS resolver (`dscacheutil -flushcache`); Amplify deleting records by name when a legacy association is removed later (handled in P6-07).

## Needs Ryan
Go/no-go, each legacy zone write, the deploy, the visual and sign-in checks.

## Common rules (Phase 6, PPY-7d8cd0)
- Read /Users/home/Projects/Papyrus/AGENTS.local.md first. Assert the account with `aws sts get-caller-identity --query Account --output text` before EVERY call: profile legacy = 335163751677, profile papyrus-production = 712236451410. Never use papyrus-development; papyrus-staging (494166748521) is not used by this phase.
- Every write needs Ryan's explicit yes in chat for that step. Legacy is READ-ONLY except the steps this ticket names (each with a yes). No SCPs on legacy; never risk legacy access; no `cdk deploy` and no `ampx` against the legacy stacks of these sites.
- Never print secret values (names only; SSM values move by pipe, never to the terminal or a ticket). Ryan deletes retired resources. Do not touch Anth.us production d2hbn1ig6nqyhy or the other anth.us apps (apricity d2n7w4kwqyfwn4, babulus d3epcqvzbxdaq, tactus dfkbdffs2viq8, primus divicqm3nhcwt).
- Baselines and scratch live under /Users/home/Projects/.baselines/phase6-<date>/ (outside any repo); clones go under /Users/home/Projects/ and are deleted afterwards (disk is tight). Only kbs writes in the Papyrus checkout (never git add/commit there); never `git stash`.
- The committed infra/site.json in each site repo still describes the LEGACY stack until the cutover ticket; production deploys use an out-of-repo, domain-free copy (as PPY-aa93b3 did for p.apyr.us).
